title: World models from drone trajectories
alt: Multi-agent trajectory prediction on an overhead inD intersection scene
summary: Learning interaction-aware, multimodal traffic dynamics from overhead observations of vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians.
description: I explore site-centric world models that represent an entire traffic scene through interacting road users. The GP-RSSM line combines a graph-conditioned recurrent state-space model with a second-order neural ODE decoder and multimodal motion hypotheses. The aim is to model both interaction dynamics and uncertainty, while distinguishing observation-conditioned prediction from self-conditioned rollout.
contribution: Graph-based temporal modeling, physically grounded trajectory decoding, and evaluation under full, partial, and prior-only observation grounding, using drone trajectory datasets including inD, rounD, and highD.
scope: The animation is a qualitative prediction example on inD, not evidence of closed-loop control performance. World model here refers to trajectory-level traffic dynamics, rather than photorealistic video generation.
caption: Prediction visualization from the GP-RSSM research code. Scene imagery and trajectories: inD / levelXdata.
secondary_alt: Graph-RSSM framework with interaction graph encoder, latent rollout, physical decoder and mixture fusion
secondary_caption: Graph-RSSM architecture from the author's trajectory world-model manuscript materials.
cv: Develop graph-conditioned recurrent state-space models with neural ODE motion decoding; evaluate multimodal prediction and observation-grounded versus self-conditioned rollout on drone trajectory data.

title: Understanding why closed-loop rollouts fail
alt: Four-regime diagnostic independently switches logged versus policy actions and target versus predicted graphs
summary: Separating action-source shift, interaction-graph changes, and the timing of error accumulation in multi-agent forecasting.
description: Accurate forecasts under logged inputs can deteriorate when a model consumes its own predictions. This study independently switches action and graph sources, then uses prefix interventions and matched-error temporal controls to investigate where the rollout gap originates and when it develops.
contribution: A paired four-regime diagnostic, early-step replacement experiments, and temporal error controls. In the audited model family, action-source shift and early error accumulation explain much of the measured rollout gap; these findings are evaluated within the specified checkpoints and data protocol.
scope: The interventions diagnose model-internal behavior. They do not establish real-world causal effects or certify a planner's safety.
caption: Four-regime protocol from the working manuscript, Where Closed-Loop Rollouts Break: Action-Source Shift and Early Error Compounding in Multi-Agent Forecasting.
cv: Design paired action/graph source-switch diagnostics and temporal controls to investigate distribution shift and early error compounding in autoregressive multi-agent rollouts.

title: From predictive validity to decision utility
alt: Future-free action candidate ranking: past observations, fixed action bank, model scoring, choice lock, then reference evaluation
summary: Testing whether a traffic dynamics model can rank available actions, rather than only predict a recorded future.
description: This work studies the gap between predictive accuracy and action-selection usefulness. Selectors receive the same action candidates built from observed history, lock their choices before reference evaluation, and are compared on recording-disjoint data. The protocol includes analytic motion anchors, learned controls, and explicit checks against future-information leakage.
contribution: A controlled candidate-ranking pipeline, rank-fidelity and regret measurements, and certificate-transfer tests. The study finds that improved closed-loop prediction does not consistently translate into better candidate ranking under the audited reference.
scope: Driving-quality scores are simulator-relative surrogates. They are not on-road safety estimates, and the learned controls are local adaptations rather than official benchmark reproductions.
caption: Evaluation framework from the working manuscript, Validity Before Utility: Future-Free Candidate Ranking with Audited Traffic Dynamics Models.
cv: Build recording-disjoint, future-free candidate-ranking audits with fixed candidate banks, analytic baselines, leakage checks, rank fidelity, and reference-relative regret.

title: ProSafeAV: world models meet tail-risk modeling
alt: ProSafeAV conceptual architecture connects a world model, reinforcement learning and an extreme-value risk model
summary: Connecting imagined traffic outcomes, surrogate safety measures, and extreme value theory for risk-aware driving research.
description: ProSafeAV explores a world-model-based reinforcement-learning framework that incorporates traffic-conflict indicators and extreme value theory. The research asks how predicted traffic interactions and tail-risk information can support proactive driving decisions. Implementation work uses a CARLA-based simulation environment and Dreamer-style latent dynamics.
contribution: Research on the interface between latent prediction, surrogate safety indicators, tail-risk estimation, and policy learning. The project connects my earlier traffic-safety work with my current focus on world models.
scope: The figure describes the research framework. Ongoing simulator experiments and journal-development work are distinct from the 2025 conference record; no real-world safety guarantee is implied.
caption: Conceptual framework from the author's ProSafeAV manuscript materials.
cv: Study world-model-based reinforcement learning with traffic-conflict indicators and extreme value theory; develop and evaluate the approach in CARLA-based simulation. Conference work listed at TRB 2025.

title: Safety assessment from forecasted trajectories
alt: Observed history and focal forecasts feed a leakage-controlled pipeline for pairwise surrogate safety diagnostics
summary: Examining how trajectory prediction errors and information boundaries affect traffic-conflict and tail-risk diagnostics.
description: This research connects black-box multi-agent forecasting with surrogate safety assessment. A leakage-controlled pipeline converts predicted motion into pairwise conflict indicators and event-level diagnostics, making the information available to the predictor explicit.
contribution: Protocol development and pilot diagnostics across overhead traffic datasets, including time-to-collision, closest-approach, and required-deceleration indicators, event identification, and tail behavior.
scope: This is ongoing protocol and pilot work. PET/MTTC components in the framework include proxy diagnostics; broader model comparisons and publication-grade tail-risk validation remain development goals.
caption: Protocol figure from the author's working manuscript on leakage-controlled surrogate safety assessment.
cv: Develop leakage-controlled pipelines from predicted trajectories to traffic-conflict indicators, event-level diagnostics, and tail-risk analysis.

title: Behavioral validity and cross-site generalization
summary: Studying which aspects of real traffic a calibrated simulator or learned model actually preserves.
description: My recent work extends the evaluation question to calibrated traffic microsimulation and cross-site trajectory models. One line separates support, interaction selection, marginal distributions, and dependence in behavioral validity. Another compares graph-based and autoregressive learners across roundabout datasets under common information and map contracts.
contribution: Layered behavioral diagnostics for calibrated twins and a common evaluation pipeline for graph-GRU, graph-RSSM, and token-autoregressive models across rounD and openDD.
scope: These are ongoing studies. Observational realism, simulator-relative counterfactual evaluation, and real-world causal validity are treated as different questions.
cv: Investigate layered behavioral validity in calibrated microsimulation and cross-site evaluation of graph-based and autoregressive traffic models.
